title: Agents on ComfyUI: tools, verification, side-effect safety

questions.q: According to the lesson, what are the three specific checks performed by the verification function Verify(G) to ensure a graph is structurally sound?
questions.answer: Type Validity, Input Completeness, and Link Integrity (plus Acyclicity).
questions.why: The 'Under the hood' section lists four checks: 1. Type Validity, 2. Input Completeness, 3. Link Integrity, and 4. Acyclicity. The question asks for the checks, and these are the explicit components of the verification function.

questions.q: In the context of the lesson's nautical chart analogy, what does 'Provisioning' refer to?
options: Checking if the route loops back on itself
Ensuring every node has its required inputs present
Verifying that all node class_types exist in the specification
Ensuring the main UI thread is not blocked
questions.answer: Ensuring every node has its required inputs present
questions.why: The 'The intuition' section states: '2. Provisioning: Does every ship (node) have the supplies it needs? (Are all required_inputs present?)'

questions.q: Which function in the `script_examples` folder is used to fetch execution history and metadata to verify that the execution state matches expectations?
questions.why: The 'In ComfyUI' section states: 'The get_history(prompt_id) function fetches the execution history and metadata, which is essential for verifying that the execution state matches our expectations.'

questions.q: Why is the verification process described as 'static analysis' rather than execution?
questions.answer: It does not execute the nodes; it only inspects the structure to ensure the graph is sound before acting.
questions.why: The 'Under the hood' section explicitly states: 'This is a static analysis. It does not execute the nodes; it only inspects the structure. This is crucial for safety: we verify before we act.'

questions.q: According to the 'Common mistakes' section, what is a key limitation of the verifier regarding the execution order of nodes?
options: It automatically sorts the nodes in topological order for execution.
It ensures there are no cycles but does not sort the nodes, requiring a separate topological sort for execution.
It executes the nodes in the order they are defined in the JSON.
It prevents all runtime errors by simulating the execution.
questions.answer: It ensures there are no cycles but does not sort the nodes, requiring a separate topological sort for execution.
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section, point 3, states: 'The verifier ensures there are no cycles, but it does not sort the nodes. When you execute the graph, you must still perform a topological sort to determine the execution order.'
